newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Final cost of Kirishi hydro-cracker seen $1.3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Final cost of Kirishi hydro-cracker seen $1.3 bln.

text.p: The final cost of installing a hydro-cracking unit at Russian refinery OOO Kirishinefteorgsintez would be around $1.3 billion, the financial director told Reuters in an interview late on Tuesday.

Nikolai Laptev said the refinery, also known as KINEF, was aiming to raise $750 million from companies and banks in the West, but that once servicing the debt and other costs were included, the final cost would almost double.
"The initial cost is around $750 million, which in itself is very expensive," Laptev said. "But the final cost will be about $1.3 billion including all extra payments."
Laptev said the refinery was holding preliminary talks with western banks and companies, declining to give any details on the discussions.
But a recent edition of specialist Russian trade publication "The Market for Oil and Gas Equipment in the CIS" said KINEF was in talks with Germany's Deutsche Bank.
Laptev said raising cash for a new hydro-cracking unit was KINEF's priority project, and that without it operations at the refinery, one of Russia's largest, could start to lose money.
"Without this hydro-cracker, life will get worse and worse," he said. "In four years, if we do not get it, this refinery will not be profitable. At the moment it is making a profit."
Kirishi is one of a number of major oil refineries in Russia looking for foreign partners to finance expensive upgrade projects.

Refineries, mostly operating well below capacity, want to boost output of light-end oil products like gasoline to earn more on the domestic and export markets. Heavy product fuel oil currently dominates Russian refinery output.
But raising cash has proved difficult, and the process is likely to be a slow one.

The fact that Kirishi, one of Russia's most efficient refineries and strategically located in northwest Russia, is having difficulties breaking even, underlines the extent of the problems faced by the refining industry as a whole.
KINEF processed 15.3 million tonnes of oil in 1996, 10 percent below its nameplate capacity of around 17.0 million tonnes. The refinery plans to boost throughout to 16.2 million tonnes in 1997.
By far its most important product in terms of volume is fuel oil. Last year heavy fuel oil and bunker fuel accounted for almost six million tonnes of products.

A new hydro cracking unit would process 4.8 million tonnes of fuel oil a year, yielding 3.5 million tonnes of light products, Laptev said, adding that the unit would take around four years to construct.
